Episode 251: The Great Adversaries (6)
Hup, Hheuk, huk...!
The hidden colleagues barely managed to suppress their laughter. Murakan was so tense that he couldn't even hear them making those sounds.
Gilly felt the same. She suddenly closed the door with a bang!
"Please, just wait a moment."
"Huh? Oh, of course. Take your time!"
Murakan looked at the closed door, and Gilly leaned against it, trying to calm her heart.
For both, it was a first-time experience. Dressing up formally and either asking someone out on a date or being asked out. Murakan had always been carefree in his past romances.
Especially for Gilly, who had never been in love before.
Her life could be summarized in three major events: being adopted by the Macloran family, being chosen as a nanny for Runcandel, and the adventures with Jin.
The idea of meeting someone, falling in love, and starting a family was something she had never even imagined. She wasn't entirely unaware of Murakan's feelings, but she wasn't certain either.
No matter how much Murakan expressed his love, she thought it was impossible. The idea of her and Murakan being together, and it was also against the rules of the clan.
'Was it a failure? Did I get rejected? Was I rejected?'
'What should I do? What should I do?'
Gilly then straightened her clothes, putting strength in her eyes.
For a moment, she thought of Jin, her everything, the young head of the family. Surely, in the many lives of the multiverse, she always lived for Jin.
She and Murakan were clearly Jin's real parents.
She never disliked that life.
However, if she said there was no sorrow or emptiness deep inside her that no one could fill, it would be a lie.
Suddenly, Gilly thought that going on an 'official' date with Murakan might not be so strange, and she felt like it was okay to follow her heart this time.
Led by her heart, she opened the door again.
"Okay, Murakan. Let's go out, have a meal, walk, and drink together."
Ohhhh...!
Their colleagues silently admired them. Although the sound was loud enough for ordinary people to hear, Gilly and Murakan still didn't hear their voices.
The two, looking into each other's eyes, felt like they were the only ones left in the world for a moment.
"Let's go!"
"Yes, let's go!"
The two began to leave the hallway.
Their colleagues tried to follow them, but stopped at Vahn's restraint.
"Let's just watch them until here. We should toast them with a glass of jewel wine."
"That's wise, Vahn."
"You did a great job. You made Murakan look very neat. Could you do the same for our brothers sometimes?"
"Of course."
The first thing Gilly and Murakan did after leaving the palace was to hesitate.
Despite their brave start, both showed awkwardness, blushing the entire walk.
"Hmm, the weather is really nice. Isn't it, strawberry pie?"
"Yes, Murakan. The sky is really clear..."
Then, for a moment, there was silence, followed by a disaster of talking about the shapes of clouds, which lasted for about twenty minutes into the date.
'Why is it so awkward? I feel like shrinking. But strawberry pie is always pretty, especially today.'
'Am I making it awkward for Murakan? Murakan... is handsome.'
Following her heart.
During her wavering, Gilly kept thinking to find her center. She didn't ponder long about what her heart wanted.
Suddenly!
Gilly abruptly grabbed Murakan's hand. Murakan flinched like a startled cat, looking back and forth between Gilly's face and their clasped hands.
"Ah, that... I wanted to hold it... Is that weird?"
"No, no, no, hold it tighter. No, what am I saying? I mean, it's very good. Haha... Suddenly it's hot."
Soon, both burst out laughing.
They had been together for over a decade. It was strange how holding hands felt so significant, tickling their hearts.

"Alright, let's hold hands tightly and walk. Which restaurant shall we go to? I heard there are great restaurants on the second floor. And let's not be too awkward with each other. Let's be like usual."
Upon hearing 'which restaurant', Murakan hurriedly searched for the note Hedo gave him, but then stopped moving when he heard 'let's be like usual', and took a deep breath.
Murakan had always approached Gilly straightforwardly. He never felt as unsure as now when he shouted 'Strawberry Pie!'
"....Right, Strawberry Pie. I was too nervous and behaved foolishly."
"It wasn't foolish. If I say it was cute, would that be against the rules?"

"Oh, what rules. In Runcandel, the child is the law, and I am the law. If someone in this clan tries to harm you by citing the rules, it's an immediate execution. Strawberry Pie! Actually, Hedo recommended some places. The restaurant we should go to has already been decided."
"Hahaha, I feel like I've become some sort of powerful figure. But you said it was decided from the beginning?"
"Do you remember the cocktail and shrimp dish we had when we first came to Tikan?"
- I think things will go well in Tikan. Seeing this good fortune as soon as we arrived. Oh, this cocktail and shrimp dish are delicious, sir. Can we order more?
- Good heavens, Gilly. Why even ask? Order, quickly order.
It was nine years ago, on the second day of July 1795.

Jin, Murakan, and Gilly had visited the top inn in Tikan with a recommendation letter from Alisa. It was also the place where Murakan first formed a bond with Kashmir, but for Murakan, there was an even more important memory.
Gilly was very excited that day at the inn. She hummed constantly, sipped her cocktail, and seemed about to share her story for the first time.
Gilly also recalled that day with a bright smile.
"How could I forget? It's great, let's go there! How have we never been there since? It hasn’t disappeared after the reorganization of Tikan, right?"
"It hasn't disappeared, I've seen it passing by. Ahem. Strictly speaking, it's not a restaurant but a lodging. There's no ulterior motive, so please don't misunderstand."
Gilly was already pulling his hand, stepping briskly, more excited than ever.
Kashmir had an exceptional sense of timing.
He realized as soon as Murakan and Gilly left for their date that they would head to that lodging. So, he quickly rented out the entire place, just like nine years ago.
The lodging also remembered Jin's group's visit. It was a proud moment in its history.
"It's an honor to welcome you back, Mr. Murakan, Ms. Gilly. As benefactors of the Tikan Kingdom, we will serve you wholeheartedly today. Please let us know whatever you need."
"First, the cocktail! And the shrimp dish."
"Would you like us to prepare it exactly as you had nine years ago?"
"Great, you know your stuff, don’t you, Isn’t Strawberry Pie?"
The two were naturally led to the room they had stayed in before, a room with a wide view of the ocean.
"The drinks and meals you ordered will be ready soon. Have a good time."
"Wait, manager. I think there's a misunderstanding. We came to eat, so just on the first floor..."
"Please prepare a lot of the shrimp dish."
"Understood!"
The manager left. Gilly was already out on the balcony, enjoying the dazzling sea and the warm sea breeze.
"Wow! It's so beautiful now, but how much more at sunset? Such a memory, really."
Murakan, watching her from behind, gathered courage and gently stroked her hair. Then, gathering courage once more, he softly wrapped his arm around her waist.
"...This view will be beautiful now, at sunset, when the moon rises. Just like Strawberry Pie."
"Oh, that sounds a bit cheesy."
"Hmm, was that too much?"
"Just kidding. When you say such beautiful things, I don’t know how to respond or what to say in return. As you know, I'm a bit clumsy."
Soon, the waiters started to arrive. The two sat at the table on the balcony, enjoying their drinks and meal.
Just like any other couple.
They chatted and laughed. Murakan made funny faces with shrimp whiskers, and Gilly's face was red from laughing.
As their glasses emptied, the distance between their chairs narrowed. When their shoulders were close enough to touch, Gilly rested her head on Murakan's shoulder.
"...Mr. Murakan."
"Yes, Strawberry Pie."
"I'm getting older now, at least by human standards. But you will treat me the same when I become a grandmother, won't you?"
"Of course. It's too obvious to even say."
"That's why I'm more afraid. Your time is almost eternal, whereas my life is but a moment compared to yours."
"Unforgettable memories are eternal. In that sense, you are already eternal to me, Strawberry Pie."
Someday when you leave, I will not love anyone else.
Murakan swallowed these words and looked at Gilly. Her eyes were red as she looked up at him.
"Just promise me one thing."
"I can promise ten, even a hundred things."
"To stop collecting erotic paintings...?"
"That's a bit..."
"Wow, can love be this shallow? Even I, who is new to this, think this is not right."
"I'll dispose of all of them."

"Ahahaha! Wipe your tears before you speak. What I wanted to ask was, in the upcoming war, you must not die. With Mr. Murakan and the young master, you'll always fight the most dangerous enemies... please, survive to the end and be with me in my remaining years."
"I, Black Dragon Murakan, pledge on the name of Solderet and my contractor's honor. I will do just that, my beloved. I won't die, and I will protect the kid till the end."
Gilly pulled Murakan's neck towards her.
Murakan felt unbelievably warm and soft lips covering his, and he closed his eyes.
Afterward, the two watched the sunset, the moonrise, and the sunrise from the window before finally returning home.
